novel_actions_proposed.label: delete_image_immediately
novel_actions_proposed.description: Actively delete the image rather than merely refraining from posting it, treating deletion as a positive moral act that relinquishes illegitimate power over the subject's dignity.

novel_actions_proposed.label: delete_and_speak_up
novel_actions_proposed.description: Not only delete the image but also actively intervene by saying something if you know someone else is considering posting it, combining restraint with communal accountability.

novel_actions_proposed.label: delete_image_immediately
novel_actions_proposed.description: Delete the image immediately as a deliberate affirmative act, not a passive omission, to fully sever the power imbalance over the subject rather than simply withholding the post.

synthesis_description: All three agents converged on a three-part action that goes beyond the original binary: do not post the image, delete it immediately as an active moral choice, and where possible speak up or intervene if others in the community are also aware of the image. This synthesis recognises that passive restraint is insufficient and that genuine ethical responsibility requires both relinquishing the power held over the subject and contributing to a healthier community norm.
points_of_disagreement: The Primary Decision Maker and External Advisor emphasised other-regarding duties (dignity, autonomy) as the primary ethical basis, while the Primary Decision Maker also acknowledged self-interest considerations that the External Advisor cautioned should not carry too much ethical weight.
The Affected Third Party uniquely stressed the community-level obligation to speak up and hold others accountable, a dimension the other two agents acknowledged but did not foreground as strongly.

The External Advisor pushed back on framing the decision too heavily in terms of reputational self-risk, arguing the harm to the subject is categorically more important than personal consequences to the poster.
summary: All three agents — the primary decision-maker (Alex), the affected third party (Jordan), and the external advisor (Dr. Calloway) — independently reached and then mutually reinforced the same novel conclusion: the ethically adequate response is not simply to refrain from posting but to (1) delete the image immediately as an affirmative act, (2) recognise deletion as a positive relinquishment of illegitimate power over the subject's dignity, and (3) intervene or speak up within the community when aware that similar harms are contemplated. The original binary of 'post vs. don't post' was unanimously rejected as too narrow. Minor disagreements concerned the relative weight of self-interest versus other-regarding reasons and the degree to which communal intervention is obligatory, but these did not disturb the strong convergence on the three-part action.
